## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of cross-lane bit manipulation and wrap-around across a 128-bit value.

- 128-bit split across two uint64 halves
- Cross-lane bit movement with shifts
- Non-branching bitwise updates

uint128 rotateLeft128_1(uint128 x) {
  uint64_t new_lo = (x.lo << 1) | (x.hi >> 63);
  uint64_t new_hi = (x.hi << 1) | (x.lo >> 63);
  uint128 r; r.hi = new_hi; r.lo = new_lo; return r;
}

## Why This Is Asked

This question assesses the ability to implement per-lane bit analytics using only shifts and masks, with zero control flow. It demonstrates understanding of SWAR (SIMD Within A Register) techniques and how to exploit bit-level parallelism within a single register.

## Key Concepts

- **SWAR (SIMD Within A Register)**: Executing multiple operations in parallel within a single register
- **Lane packing**: Organizing results into separate fields within the 128-bit struct
